original_question: Fix s. Is there a calculation of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) that is uniform for all sufficiently large primes p? In other words, for fixed Adams filtration s, does the structure of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) eventually become independent of p for large enough p, analogous to the stated behavior of Ext_A^{1,*}(F_p, F_p) for p > 2?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual wording. It correctly fixes a single Adams filtration s, asks about a uniform description of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) for all sufficiently large primes p, and uses the same motivating example from the paper that Ext_A^{1,*}(F_p, F_p) can be regarded as "independent of p" for p > 2. It also keeps the scope appropriately narrow: one fixed s, not a statement uniform in all s at once.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is Problem 3.3 in Section 3, not a conjecture or theorem elsewhere.
A should be identified as the mod-p Steenrod algebra, and the coefficient field is the prime field F_p.
s should be stated as a fixed positive integer indexing the Adams filtration; the symbol * ranges over all internal degrees.

The paper's official phrasing is "uniform calculation"; your reformulation as eventual independence of the "structure" is a reasonable gloss, but the paper does not formalize what kind of structure is meant beyond the graded Ext group on the s-line.

"For all sufficiently large primes p" should be made explicit as: there exists a bound P(s) such that the same calculation works for every prime p >= P(s). The paper does not impose any stronger uniformity requirement.
The nearby context is the Singer transfer tau_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)_{GL_s(Z/p)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_p, F_p); this is why the question is being asked.
The heuristic comparison in the paper is with Ext_A^{s,*+s}(F_p, F_p), not just Ext_A^{s,*}, and with the representation-theoretic object Hom_A^*(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)_{GL_s(Z/p)}.
The example about Ext_A^{1,*}(F_p, F_p) is presented heuristically as something that can be viewed as "independent of p" for p > 2, not as a separately stated theorem in this paper.
No additional degree restrictions, homogeneity assumptions, or nilpotency conditions belong to this problem; those appear in other sections of the paper and should not be imported here.
refined_question: Fix a positive integer s, and let A denote the mod-p Steenrod algebra. Is there a uniform calculation of the s-th Adams-filtration line Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) valid for every sufficiently large prime p (with the threshold allowed to depend on s)? Equivalently in the paper's heuristic language, for fixed s does Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) become eventually "independent of p" as p grows, in the sense suggested by the Singer-transfer comparison between Ext_A^{s,*+s}(F_p, F_p) and Hom_A^*(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)_{GL_s(Z/p)}?
justification: The draft unmistakably targets Problem 3.3: the wording "Fix s. Is there a uniform calculation of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) for all large enough p?" is essentially the paper's exact formulation. The paragraph immediately following that problem supplies the same example you used, namely that Ext_A^{1,*}(F_p, F_p) can be viewed as "independent of p" for p > 2, and it gives the intended heuristic via the comparison of Ext_A^{s,*+s}(F_p, F_p) with a representation-theoretic Hom-object. The opening sentence of Section 3 and the displayed Singer transfer map provide the hidden ambient notation and scope. There is no more formal equivalent restatement of Problem 3.3 proved in the paper, so the sharpest paper-faithful refinement is to restate Problem 3.3 with that immediate Section 3 context made explicit.
